papers.title_en: Too Smart for Its Own Good? Cognitive Fidelity and Competence Leakage in LLM Simulations of Young Learners
papers.authors: Zhen Xu, Beata Beigman Klebanov, Jamie N. Mikeska
papers.evidence: 用于教师培训和辅导的LLM学习者模拟器与认知保真
papers.tldr: LLM学习者模拟器需保持认知保真，但模型可能表现出超出设定学习者水平的知识与解题能力，即“能力泄漏”。研究分析130份师生模拟对话中的3339条学习者话语，并在五种模型配置下用四种匹配触发协议检验泄漏复现。结果显示多轮交互比孤立问答更易复发，能力更强模型复发更低，而提高推理努力未必改善保真。该工作为多轮认知保真评估提供探索性证据。
papers.abstract_en: LLM-based interactive learner simulators are increasingly used in educational applications, including teacher training and tutoring system development. A critical requirement for those simulations is cognitive fidelity: the simulated learner should maintain the assigned knowledge, misconceptions, and reasoning procedures throughout interaction. However, LLMs may express knowledge or problem-solving skills beyond the assigned learner's cognitive status, a phenomenon we refer to as competence leakage. In this exploratory study, we examine 3,339 simulated learner utterances from 130 teacher-learner simulator transcripts across three learning scenarios and identify over-competence as a prominent direction of cognitive-profile misalignment during interaction. We then investigate the recurrence of previously observed competence leakage cases under four matched-trigger evaluation protocols, ranging from isolated questioning to multi-turn interactions, across five model configurations. Overall, we observe higher violation recurrence under multi-turn protocols than under isolated question answering. More capable models generally show lower recurrence, whereas increased reasoning effort does not consistently improve cognitive fidelity and is even associated with slightly higher recurrence under multi-turn protocols in our matched-model comparison. These findings provide exploratory evidence of competence leakage phenomena in interactive learner simulation and suggest that single-turn question-answering type of evaluations alone may be insufficient, motivating the development of more systematic and reliable multi-turn protocols for evaluating cognitive fidelity in learner simulation.

papers.title_en: Silent on Code? A Computing Lens on Generative AI Guidance at Canadian Polytechnics and Research Universities
papers.authors: Marco Ho, Michael Pin-Chuan Lin, Rishva Riteshkumar Amin, Daniel Chang, Jeeho Ryoo
papers.evidence: 对高校生成式AI指导文件的文本分析
papers.tldr: 生成式AI已能编写、解释和调试代码，但高校GenAI指南多面向论文写作，计算教学缺少编程专项指引。作者分析加拿大13所理工学院与15所U15高校的公开指南，用27项编码框架覆盖治理、诚信评估、数据法律、价值观、AI素养与计算视角。结果发现课程决策多下放教师，理工学院更常默认禁止并强调就业准备，大学更重评估重构；27份指南中12份提到代码，却无机构点名AI编程助手或给出代码归属、评估、许可细则。研究提出计算学科指南五项要素并公开编码本与数据集。
papers.abstract_en: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) tools now write, explain, and debug code, which changes how computing students learn and how their work is assessed. Instructors, however, act within institutional guidance written largely with essays in mind. We report a document analysis of the public, institution-level GenAI guidance of the 13 members of Polytechnics Canada and the 15 members of the U15 Group of Canadian Research Universities, retrieved in October 2026. Using a 27-item codebook spanning governance, integrity and assessment, data and legal issues, values, AI literacy, and a computing lens, we find that both sectors leave course-level decisions to instructors, although polytechnics more often prohibit use unless the instructor permits it (8 of 13 vs. 4 of 14), and converge on disclosure, links to academic integrity policy, and, in most institutions, the expectation that programs adapt rules to their discipline. Polytechnics frame GenAI as workforce preparation substantively far more often (7 of 13 vs. 0 of 14), whereas universities more often address assessment redesign. Twelve of 27 institutions with retrievable guidance mention code, but almost always as one output type among many; none names an AI coding assistant or provides substantive code-specific guidance on attribution, assessment, or licensing. Institution-level guidance is thus not silent on code but leaves programming-specific questions largely to programs and instructors. We propose five elements of discipline-level guidance for computing and release our codebook and coded dataset.

papers.title_en: Learning the Platform, Not the Learner: Sequencing Shortcuts in the Offline Evaluation of Educational Recommender Systems and LLM Rankers
papers.evidence: 面向辅导系统与MOOC的教育推荐系统及大模型排序器的离线评估
papers.tldr: 教育推荐系统常以离线预测下一活动来比较，但下一活动多由平台、教师或引擎决定，模型可能只学到平台序列捷径。作者在五平台八数据集上，将仅用上一活动的结构预测器与十个个性化推荐器和0.5–7B开源LLM排序器对比。结构预测器达到最佳准确率的0.81–1.00（中位0.95），个性化方法仅部分数据集显著提升，LLM在合理负样本下接近随机。作者据此提出按结构意外性加权测试步骤，恢复离线准确率与实用性的联系，并发布评估清单和Python包。
papers.abstract_en: Educational recommenders are usually compared offline, by how well they predict the next activity in logs of tutoring systems, learning applications and MOOCs, where the next activity is largely decided by the platform: teachers assign problem sets, tutors draw problems until mastery, engines select questions. On eight public datasets from five platforms, we compare four structural predictors, which use nothing about the learner beyond the last activity, with ten personalised recommenders and with open-weight LLM rankers from 0.5 to 7 billion parameters, under two protocols. The structural predictors reach between 0.81 and 1.00 of the best accuracy of any method (median 0.95), mostly through population transitions rather than the course order; the best personalised recommender is significantly better on five datasets, by 0.007 to 0.102 NDCG@10, and on Eedi in three of four training runs. Every method is far less accurate on steps along transitions never seen in training and on steps chosen by learners. LLM rankers look competent with random negatives but are never much better than a word-matching baseline, and with negatives that are plausible under the course structure they stay close to random or well behind the transition heuristic, whatever their size. In a simulation with known learner needs, the structural share tracks the share of steps decided by the platform, and offline accuracy ranks an oracle of the learners' needs below imitators of the platform. Weighting test steps by how unlikely the structure makes them restores much of the link with usefulness and, on the real data, reveals a significant personalisation signal on seven of the eight datasets. We propose a syllabus-aware evaluation checklist and release a Python package that reports the lift of any recommender over the structure.

papers.title_en: Designing an Integrated Learning Ecosystem for Introductory Python Programming: Scaffolded Problem Solving, Tablet-Inspired Navigation, and AI-Enhanced Instruction
papers.evidence: 面向Python课程的AI增强一体化学习生态系统
papers.tldr: 入门 Python 课程需要学生完成问题表征、程序编写与调试，并在新情境中迁移计算概念，教学工具与脚手架容易碎片化。本文对一门含 16 个实验的课程中的 18 件教学制品做以制品为中心的设计分析，覆盖导航、脚手架、迁移、调试、AI 集成与评估。15 个脚手架实验共享七要素结构，第 16 个实验改为基于 Pygame 的综合性作业，由此提炼出四类相互关联的设计特征。研究还指出工具碎片化、可访问性、界面干扰、学生自主性与 AI 过度依赖等未解张力，为后续实证评估提供了透明先例。
papers.abstract_en: Introductory programming requires students to represent problems, develop and test programs, debug errors, and apply computational ideas in new contexts. In this paper, we present an artifact-centered design analysis of an integrated learning ecosystem developed for a 16-lab introductory Python course. The analyzed corpus comprises 18 instructional artifacts: the course syllabus, a tablet-inspired homepage, and Labs 1-16. We examined course navigation, problem representation, scaffolding, independent transfer, application development, debugging, AI integration, and assessment. All 15 scaffolded labs shared seven elements: input-processing-output (IPO) reasoning, instructor-guided programming, an independent task, a Google Colab/Gradio extension, debugging support, a task checklist, and submission requirements. Lab 16 departed from this structure as an integrative Pygame-based Hallmark Assignment. The analysis identifies four connected design features: a navigation layer that coordinates multiple tools; two forms of transfer, from guided to independent problems and from console programs to interactive interfaces; distinct roles for instructor-side AI-enhanced communication and student-side AI assistance; and a transition from repeated scaffolds to integrative problem solving. The case also identifies unresolved tensions involving tool fragmentation, accessibility, interface distraction, student authorship, and overreliance on AI. Because student learning outcomes were not examined, we make no claims about instructional effectiveness. Instead, the paper offers a transparent design precedent and identifies priorities for future empirical evaluation. Demo - https://xinxingwu-uk.github.io/COS107_Demo/Homepage/index.html Source codes - https://github.com/xinxingwu-uk/Course_Integrated_Learning_Ecosystem

papers.title_en: Can AI Understand Indonesian Children's Book Illustrations? Compliance, Safety, and the Cultural Alignment Gap
papers.authors: Rian Adam Rajagede, Rochana Prih Hastuti, Fitri Hasanah Amhar
papers.evidence: 视觉语言模型评估与生成教育儿童书籍插图
papers.tldr: 儿童书籍插图需符合发展、教学与文化规范，但AI正进入童书出版流程。研究以印尼《图书分级指南》为政府评估框架，考察视觉语言模型在合规、安全与文化对齐三项标准上的表现。结果显示，VLM在显性合规与安全判断上可靠，却系统漏掉人类评审标记的文化不适内容；AI生成插图也有同样盲点。该工作揭示了AI童书评估与生成中的文化对齐缺口。
papers.abstract_en: Children's book illustrations carry developmental, pedagogical, and cultural responsibilities that are often formally codified in guidelines. As AI systems begin entering children's publishing pipelines, both as evaluators and as generators, a natural question arises: can they reliably meet the structural, safety, and cultural standards required? We investigate this across three criteria: guideline compliance, safety, and cultural alignment, using Indonesia's Book Leveling Guideline as a government-issued evaluation framework with explicit visual criteria for four reading levels. To understand how well VLMs can identify and apply these guideline criteria, we first evaluate them on real published children's book pages and compare their assessments against a human baseline. To then examine whether AI-generated illustrations meet the same standards, we apply the VLM judge to images produced by two generation models and cross-check them against a subset of human illustrator raters. We find that VLMs are reliable on explicit criteria such as compliance and safety, but fall short on cultural alignment, systematically missing content that human raters flag as culturally inappropriate. AI-generated illustrations show the same blind spot: they satisfy structural and safety criteria but fail to capture implicit cultural details that human raters consistently identify.

papers.title_en: An Embedded Ergonomic Posture Monitoring and AI-Assisted Home Learning System on a Raspberry Pi 3B Edge Platform
papers.authors: Truyen T. Le, Vinh Dang Ngoc, Thai Bao Huynh
papers.evidence: 具备姿态监测与教学支架的嵌入式AI辅助家庭学习系统
papers.tldr: 家庭自主学习常伴随坐姿不良、久坐超时与手机分心，且缺少实时教学引导。本文在树莓派3B上构建低成本、保护隐私的边缘系统，用MediaPipe Pose与OpenCV在本地实时监测躯干、头部与肩部姿态，配合有限状态机统计学习时长、强制休息并检测手机使用，同时接入多模态AI导师给出苏格拉底式提示。原型实测端到端延迟244-250毫秒、躯干角误差4.39度MAE、内存320MB，验证了资源受限边缘部署的可行性。
papers.abstract_en: During independent home study sessions, students frequently sustain improper sitting postures, accumulate excessive sedentary hours, and experience productivity loss from off-task digital distractions. Furthermore, learners often lack real-time pedagogical scaffolding for demanding self-study curricula. To mitigate these ergonomic and instructional challenges, this paper presents an affordable, privacy-preserving cyber-physical embedded system for domestic study spaces. Engineered on a Raspberry Pi 3 Model B (1 GB RAM) paired with a UVC optical camera and a USB condenser microphone, the system executes on-device computer vision utilizing MediaPipe Pose and OpenCV to monitor upper-body alignment, sagittal head inclination, and coronal shoulder asymmetry in real time without persisting raw video streams. A deterministic finite state machine (FSM) quantifies active study durations, enforces health-compliant rest periods, and detects illicit smartphone usage. Simultaneously, an integrated multimodal AI tutoring agent parses voice and text queries via an encrypted API gateway, synthesizing Socratic conceptual hints rather than direct solutions. A lightweight parental web dashboard delivers encrypted session analytics and scheduling configurations. Empirical benchmarks on the physical prototype confirm an end-to-end inference latency of 244-250 ms at a 352x288 resolution (4.0-4.1 FPS), a trunk-angle estimation error of 4.39 degrees MAE over 5,760 synthetic ground-truth poses, a resident set size of 320 MB, a peak SoC temperature of 58.0 degrees Celsius under sustained load, and a 1.58 s total latency for the offline TTS feedback path, proving high practicality for resource-constrained edge deployment.

papers.title_en: The Linguistic Knowledge Benchmark: Do Language Models Know the Foundations of Early-Grade Literacy?
papers.authors: Maxime Lelièvre, Alasdair Mackintosh, Dominic Andrews, Tobias Murray, Moritz Boos, Oliver G. B. Garrod
papers.evidence: 评测语言模型是否掌握早期读写教学基础知识的基准
papers.tldr: 低收入国家教学语言在模型训练数据中代表性不足，需检验模型是否具备早期读写所需语言知识。作者构建语言知识基准与自动化流程，把课程文件、教师指南和课本转为覆盖九领域七等级的审核题库，并在斯瓦希里语和英语评测大量模型。前沿模型两语准确率均超90%，但小型低成本模型骤降，斯瓦希里语更差；移动端可部署模型均值仅英语47%、斯瓦希里语24%。这表明低资源课堂最实用的模型反而最弱，作者公开样例、提示词、代码与排行榜。
papers.abstract_en: Many languages of instruction in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) are poorly represented in the data used to train language models. Before these models can support early-grade literacy in such languages, we need to know whether they hold the linguistic knowledge of each language that literacy teaching relies on. To test this, we present the Linguistic Knowledge Benchmark and the reproducible, largely automated pipeline that turns curriculum documents, teacher guides and pupil books into a vetted question set organised on a fixed grid of nine linguistic domains and seven grade levels. The pipeline combines LLM-driven source survey, feature consolidation, item generation and quality control with an item-selection step inspired by item response theory and a final expert review. We instantiate it for Kiswahili (Kenya; 135 items) and English (United Kingdom; 137 items) and evaluate 121 and 119 models respectively. Frontier models exceed 90% accuracy in both languages, but accuracy falls steeply for smaller and cheaper models, and more so in Kiswahili. The two best models under 10 billion parameters reach 91.7% and 73.0% in English but only 51.9% and 40.7% in Kiswahili, and the mean accuracy of models deployable on mobile and tablet hardware is 47% in English against 24% in Kiswahili. The models most practical for low-resource classrooms are therefore the least capable in the languages they would serve. We release a 20-item sample per language, all pipeline prompts, open-source code, and a public leaderboard. This is the first rung of a three-level evaluation ladder for measuring and generating decodable text to support foundational literacy.
